q2_gaps: a calendar-placement light verb ('Lantern-night falls at midwinter'): the light-verb-over-event-noun rule names only occurred / happened / took place, so nothing explicitly licenses treating temporal 'falls at/on <time>' the same way instead of reifying a fall event

a season / period time constant ('midwinter'): the Time term inventory is Year / Month / Day / Weekday / Hour / Minute plus day-parts, deictics and fiscal periods, with no form given for a bare named season or mid-season point
notes: Reading 'falls' as temporal occurrence and hanging Time directly on the named event rather than reifying a fall event is the coherent reading and the closest analogue in the instruction set. The name is one opaque symbol with no modifier genus, the Name string preserves the hyphenated surface form, the kind atom is read off the kind word inside the name, and the absent tense atom is correct for an unanchored habitual present.
